about.title: I like the space between
paragraphs: I’m drawn to complicated things that don’t need to feel complicated. My work connects product thinking, visual design, and front-end craft to make everyday experiences a little more human.
I enjoy getting my hands into the details: finding the structure, trying a few directions, and staying close to the build.
about.principlesLabel: Things I believe about the work

principles.title: Ask better questions.
principles.text: I start with the person on the other side of the screen. What are they trying to do, and what is getting in their way?

principles.title: Make the idea tangible.
principles.text: Sketches, prototypes, and working code turn assumptions into something we can actually discuss and improve.

principles.title: Care about the last 10%.
principles.text: The empty state, the loading moment, the handoff. Small details are often where a thoughtful product earns trust.

projects.title: Field Notes
projects.description: A calmer research workspace that turns scattered observations into useful product decisions.
projects.overview: Field Notes explores how product teams can keep the nuance of raw research without losing the speed of a shared workspace. The system connects observations, themes, and decisions without forcing every study into the same rigid template.
outcomes: Reduced the path from note to insight
Tested the workflow with a clickable prototype

projects.title: Common Ground
projects.description: An identity and digital home for a neighborhood initiative built around shared local resources.
projects.overview: A warm, practical identity system for an initiative that helps neighbors share spaces, tools, and time. The work spans positioning, visual language, service touchpoints, and a small editorial website.

projects.title: Signal / Noise
projects.description: A focused monitoring tool that helps small teams see the changes that actually need attention.
projects.overview: Signal / Noise is a dashboard concept designed around attention rather than volume. It groups related changes, explains why they matter, and gives teams a calmer way to move from notification to action.

projects.title: After Hours
projects.description: An editorial archive for conversations with people who keep making things after the workday ends.
projects.overview: An independent editorial experiment about creative lives that do not fit neatly into job titles. Each issue pairs a long-form conversation with studio fragments, reading lists, and process notes.
outcomes: Balanced long-form reading with visual pacing

hobbies.moveLabel: Move {title} card; use arrow keys to reposition

items.label: Photography
items.detail: Walking without a destination, collecting shopfronts, passing gestures, and the small evidence people leave behind. Photography keeps my attention honest: notice first, explain later.

items.label: Long rides
items.description: The longer road to a distant tea stop.
items.detail: The best reset I know: choose a distant tea stop, take the longer road, and let the useful thoughts arrive late. Distance has a way of making difficult problems less dramatic.

items.label: Albums, in order
items.description: Side A, pause, then side B.
items.detail: I still like records as complete objects: sequence, cover, liner notes, and the pause before side B. Shuffle has its place, but listening in order reveals the decisions between the songs.

items.label: Cooking for people
items.detail: Recipes are useful scaffolding. The real pleasure is adjusting by smell, feeding a table, and trying to remember what changed when everyone asks how to make it again.

items.label: Marginalia
items.detail: Essays, speculative fiction, design history, and books with enough room around the sentences to argue in the margins. A good underline is a conversation postponed.

items.label: Video games
items.detail: I like games that make a world feel coherent: a tiny rule set, a surprising consequence, and just enough room to get lost. They are little laboratories for curiosity and atmosphere.

items.label: Loose sketches
items.detail: A page of bad drawings is often the shortest route to one useful shape. I sketch interfaces, rooms, machines, and whatever is nearby when a thought needs somewhere to land.

items.label: Film nights
items.detail: A film night is part cinema, part ritual: dim lights, a shared bowl of something, and a story that stays in the room after the credits.
